newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak to sell some units for 120 mln rand.
newsitem.headline: Malbak to sell some units for 120 mln rand.

text.p: Malbak Ltd said on Thursday the sale of three of its unlisted units would generate more than 120 million rand.
Acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said in a statement the sales of Eagle Freight and Stalcor had been concluded, and the sale of Tedelex agreed in principle.
"...These transactions will generate in excess of 120 million rand, in line with our expectations, and other disposals are in their final stages of negotiation," Beningfield said.
The disposals form part of Malbak's decision to unbundle its assets in a bid to unlock the value of its underlying investments.
Beningfield said the proceeds from the sale of Malbak's unlisted assets was expected to exceed 700 million rand, as previously communicated to shareholders.
Despite ongoing discussions with parties interested in buying Malbak's listed subsidiaries, Malbak had decided to distribute the shares it owns in these subsidiaries to shareholders.
Beningfield said discussions with potential buyers would not affect the distribution of shares.

"The intention is that any transaction arising out of such discussions would only be implemented after the unbundling has been completed and the preference would be that a similar offer should be made to all shareholders of such listed subsidiary."
Regarding Malbak's interest in Haggie Ltd, Beningfield said a decision could only be finalised once discussions with Haggie's joint controlling shareholder was concluded.

On London-listed MY Holdings plc, Beningfield said although there had been interest in Malbak's stake in the U.K-based company no discussions were taking place. Alternative structures were being evaluated to see if Malbak shareholders could retain their effective interest in MY.
Any such structure would be subject to approval by the South African Reserve Bank, he said.
The distribution of Malbak's holdings in its listed subsidiaries would be pro rata to shareholding and based on the number of shares held by Malbak in those companies.

For a person holding 1,000 Malbak shares, the distributions were likely to be 112 shares in Foodcorp Ltd, 612 shares in Kohler Ltd, 138 shares in South African Druggists Ltd, 140 in Ellerine Ltd and 373 in New Clicks Ltd.
Malbak shareholders would also receive a cash payment resulting from the net cash realised from the sale of the unlisted firms and other assets after settling liabilities and other costs.
Payment would only be made after the distribution was completed which was expected to be at the end of March next year.
